Material Selection for Kansas Conditions

Haysville's 37 freeze-thaw cycles per year make material durability non-negotiable. We specify exterior materials proven to withstand repeated expansion and contraction—fiber cement siding, architectural shingles with proper underlayment, and flashing systems that maintain integrity through temperature extremes. Vinyl products require careful selection for UV resistance under Kansas sun exposure, and we avoid materials that become brittle during those -5°F winter nights.

Interior finishes receive equal attention. Drywall installation follows best practices for minimizing nail pops and seam cracks common when new framing lumber acclimates to Kansas humidity levels. We allow proper curing time for concrete foundations before framing, reducing differential settling between your existing home and new addition. These timeline considerations add days to construction schedules but prevent callbacks and warranty issues that plague rushed projects.

Windows and doors represent significant thermal bridge points where conditioned air escapes. We install properly flashed units with attention to air sealing details that many contractors overlook. When you're heating and cooling additional square footage, these details directly impact your utility bills. Our hands-on approach means project supervisors personally inspect these critical installations rather than discovering problems during final walkthrough.
